document.title: Wishfire CP and Progression Balance Plan
document.implementationAuthority: User approval; parent Bead ORKA-ymk with sequential child Beads
rejectionReasons: Unsafe low-level enemy burst and weak hero margin.
Pre-buff boss loss was treated as player-facing.
Opening boundary was not a full mobile-roguelite reset.
Dragon Quest reference lacked a specific title/version.

reviewDecisions: Use the revised safety-first CP and burst contract.
Make Runa and Kaja basic attacks magical.
Remove heroHPScale 2 and absorb durability into base and growth stats.
Calculate encounter CP from stats instead of using explicit row overrides.
Use full-reset session initialization and opening choices before the first scheduler action; dialogue remains independently authored.
Use routine, hard, elite, boss, and above-boss bands as harness targets.
Use Capybara Go gameplay-loop parity as the baseline with only documented Wishfire departures.
Implement through the sequential children of ORKA-ymk.

reviewAssumptions.currentStats: Provisional diagnostic data, not protected content.
approvedConstraints: Preserve one opening offer per starting hero before the first combat turn, session-long buffs, and independently authored dialogue/events.
Use Capybara Go session continuity, event order, story feed, next-step advance, and decision-gate rhythm unless a documented Wishfire departure overrides it.

inspirations.source: Dragon Quest I, original Famicom combat analysis
inspirations.claimSummary: Specialist version-specific references describe DQ I attack-versus-defence math, bounded randomness, and a rare defense-ignoring critical pattern.
inspirations.observedPattern: Legible physical attack-versus-defence pacing with infrequent dramatic critical hits.
inspirations.wishfireBorrows: Numeric feel only: small early numbers, legible physical offense-versus-defence, bounded randomness, and rare critical identity.
inspirations.wishfireChanges: Wishfire copies no DQ I formula, party model, role growth, magic balance, recovery loop, targeting, encounter curve, or CP; it uses its own smooth mitigation, burst caps, and candidate 1% 1.25x crits.
inspirations.autoplayFit: Small readable exchanges let players parse automation; rare spikes remain exciting.

inspirations.source: Dragon Quest III, original Famicom party structure
inspirations.claimSummary: Square Enix describes a party of up to four adventurers. Broader original-Famicom mechanical conclusions remain design inference.
inspirations.observedPattern: A four-member party supports legible physical, magical, defensive, and support identities.
inspirations.wishfireChanges: Wishfire copies no formulas, grind curve, inventory pressure, vocation/class system, or authored party composition.
inspirations.autoplayFit: Role contrast supports readable automated action and target philosophy.

inspirations.claimSummary: Square Enix describes next-action time as depending on Speed and action, with order visible in CTB.
inspirations.observedPattern: Speed and action delay determine effective turn access.
inspirations.wishfireBorrows: Visible CTB/action-rate reasoning and Stoic/Warrior/Tactician/Comrade AF trigger families.
inspirations.wishfireChanges: Autoplay scores Speed inside Wishfire CP and uses the locked blue-gem AF attribution.
inspirations.autoplayFit: Fast roles have real value when their individual hit is smaller.

inspirations.claimSummary: Nintendo's manual presents a combat forecast with damage, HP, and potential double attacks.
inspirations.observedPattern: Readable damage and survival forecasting before a combat commitment.
inspirations.wishfireBorrows: Forecast discipline: validate expected damage, hits-to-KO, and danger bands.
inspirations.wishfireChanges: Continuous guard formula and CP bands replace the grid, weapon, and counterattack model.
inspirations.autoplayFit: The simulator can reject encounter packs that make automated deaths opaque or unfair.

inspirations.claimSummary: Community reference documents one-of-three level-up offers, tiered event rewards, and base-plus upgrade skills.
inspirations.observedPattern: Three-choice offers establish a persistent run build with vertical upgrades.
inspirations.wishfireBorrows: Continuous-session pace, favorable player margin, opening/session power choices, event recovery, step progression, exploration gates, and behavioral parity.
inspirations.wishfireChanges: Every starting hero chooses before the first scheduler action; buffs are universal genie-magic effects and dialogue/events remain independent interruptions.
inspirations.autoplayFit: Players establish build direction before watching the party act.

inspirations.claimSummary: Community documentation describes Chapter Adventure encounters during a journey, including camps, huts, spirits, elite choices, demons, wheels, and branch choices.
inspirations.observedPattern: Chapter progression interleaves combat with exploration events and optional choices.
inspirations.wishfireBorrows: A seeded path can contain combat and distinct exploration gates.
inspirations.wishfireChanges: Wishfire uses its own genie-magic events, no copied currencies or wheel rules, and reserves recovery for story events.
inspirations.autoplayFit: Exploration landmarks create variation between automated fights.

inspirations.claimSummary: Community documentation says level-ups and Adventure events can grant skills; examples include Forest Sprite sacrifices, elite chests, Demon pacts, Angels, and wheels.
inspirations.observedPattern: Event gates can change the source or tier of a power offer.
inspirations.wishfireBorrows: Power offers may appear at level-up and exploration gates while builds persist through the session.
inspirations.wishfireChanges: Wishfire retains its per-hero opening offer and universal genie-magic buffs.
inspirations.autoplayFit: Build choices remain legible without asking for moment-to-moment combat input.

inspirations.source: Archero 2 official Google Play listing and Campaign reference
inspirations.claimSummary: The official listing advertises rarer skill choices; the community campaign reference describes 50 rooms and bosses every tenth room.
inspirations.observedPattern: A visible multi-step chapter can place planned boss milestones within a longer run.
inspirations.wishfireChanges: Capybara Go, not Archero 2, governs Wishfire's step progression and exploration gates; Wishfire uses configurable positive integer N.

damageFormula.dot: snapshot MAG * potency; no defense, variance, or crit

harness.conclusion: The patch doubled fight length and improved enemy defeats without repairing damage relationships or party outcomes.

formulaDefects: Runa and Kaja physical basics ignore their primary MAG stat.
Hero and enemy mitigation coefficients differ.
Crit multiplier depends on power and differs by side.
CP ignores MAG, RES, SPD, crit, and attack mode.
DOT bypasses ordinary mitigation and needs a separate budget.
statBudgetDefects: Enemy level-one offense spans 8 to 28 while hero basic offense spans 5 to 15.
Djinn MAG 28 produces 18 to 32 normal damage.
Defensive enemies reduce Runa and Kaja basics to one damage.
The default target CP 120 exceeds current party formula CP 89.2.
Explicit CP values are non-monotonic relative to stats.

playerFacingTerms.dire_bargain: Provisional name for an explicit power-with-cost accept/refuse offer; benefit and cost appear together.
playerFacingTerms.hobsonsChoice: Design shorthand only. The observed NPC bargain is an accept/refuse trade, not a Hobson's choice.

eventPlacement.replaceCombatStep: A standalone event consumes its own path position, starts no combat, and increments stepIndex once at completion.
eventPlacement.interruptCombatStep: Dialogue or event attached to combat pauses CTB, resumes the identical combat state, and never increments stepIndex.
eventPlacement.opening: Opening dialogue remains independently authored; all starting heroes complete cached offers before the first scheduler action.
eventPlacement.combatGate: Authored combat is selectable, mandatory, or absent. Combat and side activities return to the same session feed and route state after resolution.

determinismAndSafety.construction: Seed resolves only the step skeleton, types, and deterministic per-step seeds at initialization. On first entry, evaluate current build, prior choices, HP, and milestones using that step seed, then cache selected content or offer before presentation.
determinismAndSafety.fallback: Combat-family slots use seeded same-family fallback, then basic combat. Required exploration slots use seeded same-family fallback, then guaranteed baseline boon or treasure. Required exploration never converts to combat; shown content never rerolls.
determinismAndSafety.endConstraint: Final step is end_milestone. Each session template declares visible milestone positions; validator enforces only those declarations and final end milestone.
determinismAndSafety.milestoneSchedule: N controls session length only. A template may declare question, combat, boss, or other visible milestones at arbitrary positions, such as Day 1/6/7/15.
determinismAndSafety.combatStreak: No more than three combat-family steps consecutively; guaranteed baseline boon or treasure makes this unconditional.
determinismAndSafety.eventStreak: No more than two non-combat steps consecutively before combat-family play unless authored narrative chain permits it.
determinismAndSafety.progress: Show stepIndex/stepCount, current landmark/type, and next locked milestone.

proofMatrix.5: Opening offers, event gate, combat-family step, and end milestone finish in seed order.
proofMatrix.10: Declared milestone/end constraint, combat streak rule, and attached mid-combat dialogue pause/resume pass.
proofMatrix.15: Screenshot-parity route validates declared Day 1/6/7/15 milestones, explicit advance, combat return, and end milestone.
proofMatrix.20: Seeded branch and event selection remain stable through rerender, pause, and resume.
proofMatrix.60: Declared milestone schedule, no duplicate completion, bounded state, and final completion after step 60 pass.
proofMatrix.13: Positive-integer validation, deterministic skeleton, safe fallbacks, and final-step indexing pass.

parityChecklist: One continuous session feed persists across story, combat, and side activities.
Every resolved step exposes an explicit next-step advance before route progress changes.
Combat can be a selectable gate, a mandatory event result, or absent.
Combat and side activities return to the same session state rather than a quest ladder.
NPC bargains show benefit, cost, and accept/refuse before mutation.
Opening buff choices and AF specials use the approved Wishfire departures.
unresolvedProductDecisions: Which event types and named content ship in the first authored catalog?
May a dire bargain always be declined, or do some story branches force a cost?
Which visible milestone schedules should the first session templates declare?
What permanent rewards survive a completed or abandoned session beyond currently approved progression?
Are fated_gift and dire_bargain final player-facing names, or should genie-world narrative replace them?

contracts: Symmetric physical and magic direct-damage formula
Wishfire CP from expected threat, burst, effective HP, and action rate
Recovered Speed-based multiattack with linked scheduler insertion, full-sequence CP/burst accounting, and bounded hero-only access
Encounter construction through CP ratio bands
Per-starting-hero opening buff queue before the first scheduler action
Four-hero target philosophies, autoplay tuning, genie-world reskin, dialogue, and validation harness

directDamage.statusDamage: Burn and Venom use card-defined fixed stage values; no crit or variance.
directDamage.ownershipRationale: Wishfire-owned formula. DQ I supplies desired small-number readability only, never coefficients, progression, magic rules, party model, encounter curve, or recovery assumptions.
directDamage.burstContract: Each hostile kit declares maxSingleActionDamage and maxTargetHPFraction after all crit, variance, multi-hit, proc, action-status damage, and every strike in an uninterruptible sequence. The resolver rejects a ceiling above the actor's encounter surface.

roleSculpting.structuralReference: DQ III official four-adventurer overview informs the need for four distinct roles; Wishfire role stats, growth, targeting, kit value, CTB rate, AF, and balance are design inference.
roleSculpting.exclusions: No DQ III formulas, grind curve, inventory pressure, vocation/class system, or party composition transfers.
roleSculpting.Fara: Tank: highest DEF and durable HP, restrained direct offense; effective HP and Cover/Shield sustain carry CP.
roleSculpting.Hondo: Physical damage: highest ATK and growth, lower durability; direct damage, crit, and offensive procs carry CP.
roleSculpting.Runa: Magic control: highest MAG and growth, low-to-medium HP with RES/Speed; magic, status prevention, and delay carry CP.
roleSculpting.Kaja: Support: restrained direct damage with defensible survivability; healing, shields, ally protection, and special contribution carry CP.
roleSculpting.sameLevelRule: Roles do not require equal stat totals or equal BaseCP.

authoritativeTargetDesign.Fara_Stoic: takes hostile HP damage, including valid Cover interception
authoritativeTargetDesign.Hondo_Warrior: deals positive damage to an enemy
authoritativeTargetDesign.Runa_Tactician: successfully applies an eligible enemy status
authoritativeTargetDesign.Kaja_Comrade: a living ally takes hostile HP damage

astralFlowReview.supersedes: Historical random living-hero enemy-death orb assignment.
astralFlowReview.visualFeedback: Existing blue AF gem originates at the qualifying event, flies to the earning hero, and credits AF on arrival.

onePerActionSemantics.Fara: One after hostile action causes HP loss, including Cover; multi-hit aggregates.
onePerActionSemantics.Hondo: One after action deals any positive damage; multi-hit and AoE aggregate.
onePerActionSemantics.Runa: One after action applies at least one new eligible status.
onePerActionSemantics.Kaja: One after action causes any other living ally to lose HP.

astralFlowReview.cpRule: AF contributes only through expected special-release net value within the encounter horizon.

combatPower.authoringContract: BaseCP is absolute permanent content power derived from level, stats, and kit. Explicit CP overrides are forbidden.

terminology.level: Progression depth from EXP. It selects the expected stat band and neutral benchmark.
terminology.combatPower: Realized combat prowess or threat from actual stats, action frequency, and kit contribution.
terminology.sameLevelRule: Equal level never requires equal CP; roles may differ in HP, offense, mitigation, Speed, control, healing, AoE, and procs.

combatPower.baseCP: Derived before session buffs; used to sort and place authored content.
combatPower.currentCP: Recalculated from the same inputs after session buffs; used in live simulation and telemetry.
combatPower.neutralHit: directDamage resolver(mainOffense, benchmarkDefense, level, normal potency, normal element, neutral variance)
combatPower.ctbActionRate: clamp(SPD / 10, 0.60, 1.80); the sole ordinary Speed throughput factor.

speedMultiattack.status: Recovered historical rule retained as a target design; current code labels its automatic ratio retired.
historicalEvidence: Scripts/functionBank.js at 5944eba^: TryGrantSpeedExtraTurn grants a hero one explicit scheduler insertion when effective SPD is at least SpeedDoubleRatio times the highest living enemy SPD.
web-runner/modules/functionBank.js at 5944eba^ mirrors the same rule; state.js supplies SpeedDoubleRatio default 2.0 and ExtraTurnGranted latch.
d84fe6c labels SpeedDoubleRatio legacy; current TryGrantSpeedExtraTurn aliases skill-driven TryGrantConfiguredExtraTurn.
speedMultiattack.trigger: Living hero effective SPD >= 2.0 * highest living enemy effective SPD.
speedMultiattack.semantics: One linked explicit scheduler insertion directly after the normal action; this is not an extra hit inside that action.
speedMultiattack.sequenceCount: Derived 2 when the trigger passes, otherwise 1.
speedMultiattack.latch: ExtraTurnGranted[heroUID] blocks another grant until the current hero turn advances.
speedMultiattack.enemyAccess: Hero-only. A future enemy exception requires approved kit data and passing its encounter-surface full-sequence burst ceiling.
speedMultiattack.cpRule: ctbActionRate is multiplied by per-strike kit value times sequence count once; full linked-sequence damage supplies maxSingleActionDamage and maxTargetHPFraction.
speedMultiattack.afRule: Each separately scheduled strike may gain AF once through its role trigger; multi-hit inside either strike still gains once, so the linked sequence gains at most twice.
presentation: Grouped 2 HITS or equivalent sequence badge
Two distinct lunge, impact, and damage-text beats

kitValue.expectedDirectDamage: Expected primary-target damage per strike against the neutral defender.
kitValue.perStrikeTotal: expectedDirectDamage + critBonus + aoeBonus + sustain + control + statusProc + afContribution
kitValue.burstValue: 0.35 * maxSingleActionDamage, where maxSingleActionDamage is the full uninterruptible sequence

schema.actionMix: Array of action id, weight, and physical or magic path; weights sum to one.
schema.zeroMeans: Effect unused; missing field fails validation.
schema.measurementRule: Expected inputs are measured with the actual role-targeting policy and its recorded target distribution.
schema.burstRule: maxSingleActionDamage and maxTargetHPFraction aggregate crit, variance, multi-hit, proc, action-status damage, and every strike in one uninterruptible Speed sequence; the actor's CP surface ceiling must pass.
schema.afRule: AF source must be Stoic, Warrior, Tactician, or Comrade. Qualifying multi-hit/AoE results aggregate to one resolved action; separately scheduled Speed strikes can each qualify once; contribution is zero unless the special can release within the simulated horizon.

catalog.insertionRule: Choose targetBaseCP strictly between adjacent neighbors, tune stats or kit, then rerun simulation calibration.

workedSameLevelExample.reading: Defence and HP carry almost half of BaseCP.
Magic offense and speed create higher threat despite lower durability.

level1MixedExample.status: withdrawn; regenerate under approved safety bands

damageMatricesLevel1.doubleDigits: elite/boss only; telegraph required above 12% target max HP

acceptance.behavioralParityRationale: Capybara Go informs continuous-session pace, player advantage, event recovery, and session power choices; Wishfire owns numeric bands and validation.
acceptance.preBuffBossRule: Diagnostic only; never a player-facing loss target.

scaling.referenceScope: Capybara Go defines behavioral parity for continuous player-advantaged sessions; FFX checks CTB/action-rate and role-trigger AF; DQ I contributes small-number readability; DQ III contributes four-role structural contrast. Wishfire owns all formula, target, burst, win, recovery, and parity validation.
scaling.targetingRule: All TTK and casualty simulations use the actual role-targeting policy.
scaling.astralFlowRule: At every sampled level, each role earns 10 configurable AF only through its approved one-per-resolved-action trigger, credits special-release value only when reachable, and uses the blue gem from that event to that hero. Each separately scheduled Speed strike can qualify once; multi-hit within a strike cannot multiply AF.
scaling.speedMultiattackRule: At every sampled level, check the recovered 2.0 effective-SPD threshold, derived sequence count, linked insertion, latch, full-sequence burst ceiling, CTB throughput, integer boundaries, and no double-counting in CP.
scaling.highLevelRule: Validate bounded same-level TTK, damage-to-HP ratios, and CP relationships; do not require single-digit damage.
scaling.monotonicBaseCP: BaseCP(level + 1) must exceed BaseCP(level) for each combatant's own progression.
scaling.sameLevelRule: Same-level roles may differ in BaseCP and CurrentCP.
scaling.currentCPRule: An applied session buff changes CurrentCP in the expected direction and leaves BaseCP unchanged.
failureConditions: recovered Speed threshold has wrong sequence count or linked insertion
CTB throughput double-counts a Speed sequence
damage, burst, durability, or CP monotonicity failure

numericalReviewIssues: Current data lacks kit CP schema inputs and an authoritative role-target policy binding for the harness.
Routine win-rate suite must record no-buff, fixed Common, and seeded real-offer modes with offensive, defensive, and neutral selection policies.
Pre-buff boss evaluation is diagnostic only and never changes the player-facing opening queue.
The initial 10-AF role rate needs seed calibration against each role's trigger frequency and special horizon.
Recovery-event cadence must preserve approved retention bands because cards, inventory, and emergency healing are excluded.
User review must decide whether above-boss content ships now or remains catalog-only.

definitionOfDone: All formula owners return identical seeded results.
Canonical hero stats match approved checkpoint tables.
All enemy CP derives from current stats and compositions meet tolerance.
CP, expected damage, burst ceiling, durability, and encounter outcomes rise monotonically in their authored lanes.

Bidirectional low/high scaling, actual role-targeting, offer-mode, CP monotonicity, Speed-sequence breakpoint/count, CTB throughput, full-sequence burst, rounding/overflow, damage, win rate, TTK, casualty, and deadlock bands pass.

Each role's approved 10-AF configurable trigger is attributed exactly once per resolved action at low and high level; separately scheduled Speed strikes can each qualify once, gem origin/recipient matches credit, and AF never becomes a generic damage-dealt meter.
A qualified living hero receives exactly one linked extra scheduled action at the recovered two-times-Speed threshold; the latch prevents recursion and grouped visual feedback proves both strikes.
A full session reset completes before every starting-hero opening choice; only the first scheduler action remains blocked until choices complete.
Opening and mid-combat dialogue/event interruptions preserve and resume exact combat/session state; pause and resume restore the exact pending offer and state.
Configurable positive-integer sessions pass the N=5,10,15,20,60,13 proof matrix with declared milestones, deterministic steps, and cached choices.
Abandon clears the battle with no reward or penalty.
CP catalog, scaling-drift report, change report, and production-path evidence are attached before design-review handoff.
